question_payload.question: A block of mass $m_1$ rests on an incline of angle $\theta = 20^\circ$. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are $\mu_s = 0.8$ and $\mu_k = 0.5$. It is connected via a massless string over a massless and frictionless pulley. Block $m_2$ has mass 2 kg. If $m_1 = 1.5$kg, what's the magnitude of the acceleration of the $m_2$ (in $m/s^2$)?

solution.description:
$$F_2 = m_2 g = 19.62$$
$$F_1 = m_1 g \sin \theta = 5.032$$
The frictional force acts against $F_2$.

solution.section_title: Step 2: Determine Net Force and Acceleration
solution.description:
Since $F_2 > F_1$, the net force is calculated as:
$$a = \frac{F_{\text{net}} - m_1 g \cos \theta \mu_k - m_1 g \sin \theta + m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2}$$

files.question_html:
A block of mass {{params.m1}} kg rests on an incline of angle {{params.theta}} degrees. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are {{params.mu_s}} and {{params.mu_k}} respectively. It is connected via a massless string over a massless and frictionless pulley. Block {{params.m2}} has mass {{params.m2_mass}} kg.

If {{params.m1}} = {{params.m1_mass}} kg, what is the magnitude of the acceleration of the {{params.m2}} (in m/s2)?
files.server_py:
import random
import math


def generate(use_predefined_values=0):
    # Predefined values for testing
    predefined_values = [
        {'m1': 5, 'theta': 30, 'mu_s': 0.5, 'mu_k': 0.3, 'm2_mass': 3},
        {'m1': 7, 'theta': 45, 'mu_s': 0.6, 'mu_k': 0.4, 'm2_mass': 4},
        {'m1': 10, 'theta': 20, 'mu_s': 0.7, 'mu_k': 0.5, 'm2_mass': 8}
    ]

    # 1. Dynamic Parameter Selection
    if use_predefined_values:
        params = predefined_values[random.randint(0, len(predefined_values) - 1)]
    else:
        params = {
            'm1': round(random.uniform(1, 10), 2),       # mass in kg
            'theta': round(random.uniform(15, 45), 2),   # angle in degrees
            'mu_s': round(random.uniform(0.1, 1.0), 2),   # static friction coefficient
            'mu_k': round(random.uniform(0.1, 1.0), 2),   # kinetic friction coefficient
            'm2_mass': round(random.uniform(1, 10), 2)    # mass of block m2 in kg
        }

    m1 = params['m1']
    theta = math.radians(params['theta'])  # Convert angle to radians
    mu_k = params['mu_k']
    m2 = params['m2_mass']
    g = 9.81  # acceleration due to gravity in m/s²

    # 2. Calculate Forces
    F2 = m2 * g
    F1 = m1 * g * math.sin(theta)  # Down the incline
    F_friction = mu_k * m1 * g * math.cos(theta)  # Friction opposing the motion

    # 3. Determine Net Force and Acceleration
    if F2 > (F1 + F_friction):
        F_net = F2 - (F1 + F_friction)
        a = F_net / (m1 + m2)  # a = F_net / (m1 + m2)
    else:
        a = 0  # No acceleration if F2 is not greater than sum of forces

    # Return the structured data
    return {
        'params': {
            'm1': m1,
            'theta': params['theta'],
            'mu_s': params['mu_s'],
            'mu_k': params['mu_k'],
            'm2': params['m2_mass'],
            'm1_mass': m1
        },
        'forces': {
            'F1': round(F1, 3),
            'F2': round(F2, 3),
            'F_friction': round(F_friction, 3),
            'F_net': round(F_net, 3) if F2 > (F1 + F_friction) else 0
        },
        'correct_answers': {
            'acceleration': round(a, 3)  # Round to 3 decimal places
        },
        'nDigits': 3,
        'sigfigs': 3
    }
files.solution_html:
First, we need to determine the forces acting on both blocks in the system. For block {{params.m2}}, the force due to gravity is: $$F_2 = m_2 g = {params.m2_mass} \times 9.81$$
Let's calculate this:
$$F_2 = {params.m2_mass} \times 9.81$$ For block {{params.m1}} on the incline, the force due to gravity acting along the incline is: $$F_1 = m_1 g \sin(\theta) = {params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \sin({params.theta})$$
Calculating F1:
$$F_1 = {params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \sin({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})$$ (Note: We convert \theta from degrees to radians) The friction force is given by: $$F_{\text{friction}} = \mu_k \times F_{n_1}$$ where: $$F_{n_1} = m_1 g \cos(\theta)$$
Now we can calculate the normal force:
$$F_{n_1} = {params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \cos({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})$$
Thus, the friction force becomes:
$$F_{\text{friction}} = \mu_k \times \left({params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \cos({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\right)$$ The net force on the system can be determined from the difference between the gravitational force acting on m2 and the component of gravitational force acting on m1 along the incline: $$F_{\text{net}} = F_2 - F_1 - F_{\text{friction}}$$
Substituting in our calculations:
$$F_{\text{net}} = F_2 - F_1 - F_{\text{friction}}$$
$$ = {params.m2_mass} \times 9.81 - \left({params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \sin({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\right) - F_{\text{friction}}$$ Now, according to Newton's second law, we can find the acceleration of the system: $$a = \frac{F_{\text{net}}}{m_1 + m_2}$$ where: $$F_{\text{net}} = {params.m2_mass} \times 9.81 - \left({params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \sin({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\right) - \left(\mu_k \times \left({params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \cos({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\right)\right)$$
Finally, substituting in all values gives:
$$a = \frac{{params.m2_mass} \times 9.81 - {params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \sin({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180}) - \left(\mu_k \times \left({params.m1} \times 9.81 \times \cos({params.theta} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\right)\right)}{{params.m1} + {params.m2}}$$
The resulting acceleration of block {{params.m2}} in m/s² is:
$$a = {correct_answers.acceleration}$$
